met_analysis:
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Sri Ganganagar, Rohtak, Hardoi, Varanasi, Ranchi, Sagar Island and thence southeastwards towards Northwest Bay of Bengal and extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over North Punjab & adjoining Pakistan at 0.9 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Western parts of Gangetic West Bengal & adjoining north Jharkhand now lies over North Jharkhand and adjoining Bihar and extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The trough from North Bihar to Northwest Bay of Bengal across Jharkhand and Gangetic west Bengal between 1.5 & 3.1 Km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southwest Madhya Pradesh & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over South Odisha & neighbourhood now lies over North Coastal Andhra Pradesh & adjoining South Chhattisgarhat 5.8 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northeast Assam & neighbourhood now lies over Central Assam & adjoining Nagaland between 1.5 & 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over north Haryana & neighbourhoodextending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over East Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood between 1.5 & 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Gulf of Mannar adjoining south Tamil Nadu between 5.8 & 7.6 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in upper level westerlies with its axis at 7.6 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 70°E to the north of Lat. 30°N has moved away.
